comparisons.peer_summary: AMD provides CPUs, APUs, and chipsets for desktops and notebooks with AI capabilities and security features, and uses GPUs with software to power immersive gaming experiences.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and AMD explicitly identify 'gamers' as a core audience for their graphics and computing products, highlighting the delivery of immersive experiences. NVIDIA frames this within the context of GPUs enabling 'immersive, increasingly cinematic virtual worlds' and expanding due to creators and generative AI on PC. AMD similarly states that its GPUs 'power immersive gaming experiences for PCs' alongside CPUs and APUs that bring performance and AI capabilities to gamers and creators. While both acknowledge the convergence of gaming and AI/creator workloads, NVIDIA's disclosure specifically emphasizes the shift of generative AI to the local PC for privacy and latency, whereas AMD's summary focuses on the broader portfolio (CPUs, APUs, GPUs) driving innovation for these users without detailing the specific AI deployment dynamics.

sentences.text: Gamers choose NVIDIA GPUs to enjoy immersive, increasingly cinematic virtual worlds.

With the advent of generative AI, we expect a broader set of PC users to choose NVIDIA GPUs for running generative AI applications locally on their PC, which is critical for privacy, latency, and cost-sensitive AI applications.

We drive innovation with our line-up of CPUs, APUs and chipsets for desktops and notebooks, to bring performance, efficiency, AI capabilities and modern security features to gamers, creators, consumers and enterprises.

Our GPUs, including discrete GPUs, semi-custom SoC products and development services, work together with software to power immersive gaming experiences for PCs, game consoles and cloud gaming services.
